calls.head: Nowhere to hide for O'Reilly
calls.body: At home, the Kings keep sending Byfield’s line (Moore, Byfield and Perry) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter Laviolette has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Predators’ first line is Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque.

calls.title: Moore, Byfield and Perry barely saw the Predators’ first line
calls.plain: Los Angeles sent Moore, Byfield and Perry out against the Predators’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Laviolette sent them out against Colton, Drury and Edström (3:56 of 10:17 at 5-on-5).

calls.head: Forecheck vs. Patience
calls.body: The Kings hound the puck, but the Predators sit back. Los Angeles is near the top of the league for forecheck pressure, and Nashville is near the bottom. Expect the Kings to win more pucks back deep in the Predators’ end.
calls.call: The Kings put more forecheck pressure on than the Predators.

LAK.head: We gave Los Angeles a 60% chance, but Nashville had other ideas.

NSH.head: We had Nashville as slight underdogs (40%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Juuse Saros stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Saros stopped all 30 shots, worth 2.8 expected goals. That is more than Nashville’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 45 starts.

surprises.head: Los Angeles brought the hits
surprises.body: Los Angeles’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 170, against their usual 105 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Nothing gets past Saros
paras: Filip Forsberg struck first for the Predators early in the first, and he scored again midway through the second to make it 2-0. Adam Edström and Andre Lee squared off later in the period. Adam Wilsby added an empty-net goal with a little over two minutes left to make it 3-0.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Juuse Saros turned aside all 30 shots for the Predators, and Anton Forsberg stopped 27 of 29 at the other end. The Preds improved to 9-4-5 and climbed to third in the Central, while the Kings dropped to 5-9-2, seventh in the Pacific.

items.text: The Predators are rolling: five straight wins.
Erik Haula played his first game against Nashville since leaving.
Adam Wilsby scored his first goal of the season, his first since Dec 20, 2025 (51 games played since).
The Kings’ Mats Zuccarello was back in the lineup after missing six games.
